chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: Joe Rulo teaches him to read by position
summary: Cornetist Joe Rulo shows him a quick sight-reading method in the locker room, and he comes to find classical parts easier than jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, how did you find that you could get along in that band as far as the reading was concerned ---
Well, by this time, I was doing pretty good ---
Yeah but not good enough. And, so, Joe Rulo, who was the other cornet player in the band, said - look - if you want to really do yourself a favor -

now - he said, if you will let me--- when we're not busy doing what we have to do and you want to come in there -- in the locker room with me, I'll show you a quick way to read. And, he gave me a lot of his time.
Tell a little bit more about that, if you want to---
Well, Joe was a good hot trumpet player too; he played a lot of very good hot trumpet and he used to take me in the room and show me - so - fa - la - style reading; in other words, by position---
And, he taught me very quickly - so I could play those arrangements. I got to the point where I could play the classical things in the pit--
You know, I mean, read the classical parts because they weren't that tough; I thought classics were much easier than jazz, you know, to read.
